svg.aria-label: How to write 你: 7 strokes · 6 pen lifts · 9 movements
svg.title: Writing 你
svg.desc: 9 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 你 (chinese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansSC-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after Hanzi Writer Data 你.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–7 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/%E4%BD%A0.json>. Source note on variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 你. Medians 1–2 draw 亻 first: a left-falling stroke followed by a separately started vertical. Median 3 restarts at the upper right and falls down-left; median 4 restarts below it, crosses rightward, then hooks down-left without lifting; median 5 restarts at the centre, descends, then hooks left without lifting; medians 6–7 separately draw the lower-left dot down-left and the lower-right dot down-right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, both joined hooks, the component order, and six intervening pen lifts; Noto's right horizontal and hooks are squarer than the source medians, and stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.
